scope: Disposable acceptance candidates only; these benchmark changes are not authorized for merging into the product by this manifest.

workloads.objective: Fix the misleading Python-specific implementation wording. The coding_start tool description in src/runtime.ts and approved coding requirement notification in src/telegram.ts must describe coding implementation without claiming a particular runtime, so the same wording is accurate for Pi, Python and legacy Node jobs. Preserve the confirmation boundary, queued sandbox, draft-PR promise and duplicate/rejected notification behavior. Change only those two source files; no tests, configuration or package scripts.

Expose the exact job-pinned execution profile in coding_status detail and list results as execution: {runtime,image,models:{leader,coder,reviewer},effort}. Use persisted job settings, not current configuration/preferences. Historical missing runtime means node; missing leaderModel means the job model. Preserve the existing runtime notebook object and every existing status field. Do not return raw settings or private model inputs. Update the coding_status tool description to explain the profile is pinned and does not prove completion. Preserve owner isolation and make no writes, provider calls or job state transitions. Change only src/coding/controller.ts and src/runtime.ts, plus relevant tests if needed.

Add a read-only coding_model_usage tool with exactly {operation:'coding_model_usage',id:<job UUID>}. Integrate strict domain and global protocol schemas, JobTools dispatch, runtime tool availability/description and CodingController. Return {jobId,attemptId,total,states:{pending,complete,uncertain},roles:{leader,coder,reviewer},purposes:{agent,compaction,unknown}} for coding_model_calls belonging to the owned job and its current attempt only. Every counter is a nonnegative integer, including zero. Null attempt returns zero counts and attemptId:null. Map input.purpose 'agent'/'compaction' to their buckets; missing or other values to unknown. Never return raw input/output, messages, tokens, secrets or job settings. Reject nonexistent/foreign jobs and revoked owners. This read must not need a foreground turn, mutate data, call a provider or change job state. Expose the tool only when coding capability is enabled; describe counts as admitted call states, not verified completion, billing or useful progress. Preserve existing coding tools/approval paths and legacy runtime behavior. No database migration, dependency, infrastructure or allocation changes. Modify only the relevant src protocol/runtime/tools/coding modules and tests. Preserve normal JobTools audit receipts; the no-write restriction applies to coding jobs, attempts and model-call records.
